heading.en: Why is the rear-view mirror curved?

hook.en: The mirror on a scooter shows the whole road behind, but makes cars look farther away. A shaving mirror does the opposite. Both follow one equation.
hook.kn: ಸ್ಕೂಟರ್‌ನ ದರ್ಪಣ ಹಿಂದಿನ ಇಡೀ ರಸ್ತೆಯನ್ನು ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, ಆದರೆ ವಾಹನಗಳು ದೂರ ಕಾಣುತ್ತವೆ. ಕ್ಷೌರದ ದರ್ಪಣ ಇದರ ವಿರುದ್ಧ. ಎರಡೂ ಒಂದೇ ಸಮೀಕರಣ ಪಾಲಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

title.en: Apply f = R/2 and the mirror equation
Find magnification and nature of the image

say.en: The mirror on a scooter shows the whole road behind, but makes cars look farther away. A shaving mirror does the opposite. Both follow one equation. In this lesson: Use the Cartesian sign convention.
Apply f equals R over 2 and the mirror equation.
Find magnification and nature of the image.

body.en: All distances are measured from the pole. Distances in the direction of the incident light are positive; those against it are negative. Heights above the principal axis are positive. For a spherical mirror the *focal length* is half the radius of curvature, $f = R/2$; with this convention a concave mirror has negative $f$ and a convex mirror positive $f$.
body.kn: ಎಲ್ಲಾ ದೂರಗಳನ್ನು ಧ್ರುವದಿಂದ ಅಳೆಯಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಆಪಾತ ಬೆಳಕಿನ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನ ದೂರಗಳು ಧನ, ವಿರುದ್ಧ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನವು ಋಣ. ನಾಭಿದೂರ f = R/2.

points.en: Object distance u is negative for a real object

For a spherical mirror the focal length is half the radius of curvature, f = R/2; with this convention a concave mirror has negative f and a convex mirror positive f.

say.en: All distances are measured from the pole. Distances in the direction of the incident light are positive; those against it are negative. Heights above the principal axis are positive. For a spherical mirror the focal length is half the radius of curvature, f equals R over 2; with this convention a concave mirror has negative f and a convex mirror positive f. Object distance u is negative for a real object.
say.kn: ಎಲ್ಲಾ ದೂರಗಳನ್ನು ಧ್ರುವದಿಂದ ಅಳೆಯಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಆಪಾತ ಬೆಳಕಿನ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನ ದೂರಗಳು ಧನ, ವಿರುದ್ಧ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನವು ಋಣ. ನಾಭಿದೂರ f equals R over 2.

say.en: Concave: f is less than 0; convex: f is greater than 0.

title.en: Board: image by a concave mirror

narration.en: Let us draw a ray diagram for a concave mirror and then check it with the mirror equation.

say.en: Draw the principal axis and a concave mirror at the pole P. The focus F is halfway between P and the centre of curvature C, so f = R/2.
Put an object beyond C. A ray parallel to the axis reflects through the focus.
A ray through the focus reflects parallel to the axis. Where the two rays meet is the image: real, inverted and smaller, between C and F.
Check with the mirror equation using the sign convention: u = −40 cm and f = −15 cm.
So v = −24 cm and m = −0.6: the image is 24 cm in front of the mirror, inverted and 0.6 times the size.
Let us draw a ray diagram for a concave mirror and then check it with the mirror equation.

narration.en: Drag the tip of the object. A ray parallel to the axis reflects through the focus F (or seems to come from it, for a convex mirror); a ray to the pole reflects at an equal angle. They meet at the image: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, m = −v/u. Cartesian signs: distances to the left of the mirror are negative.
narration.kn: ಗೋಳೀಯ ದರ್ಪಣದಲ್ಲಿ ಬಿಂಬಗಳು. ಸ್ಲೈಡರ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಸರಿಸಿ, ಓದುಗಳು ಹೇಗೆ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತವೆ ಎಂದು ಗಮನಿಸಿ.

caption.en: Drag the tip of the object. A ray parallel to the axis reflects through the focus F (or seems to come from it, for a convex mirror); a ray to the pole reflects at an equal angle. They meet at the image: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, m = −v/u. Cartesian signs: distances to the left of the mirror are negative.
caption.kn: ವಸ್ತುವಿನ ತುದಿ ಎಳೆಯಿರಿ. ಅಕ್ಷಕ್ಕೆ ಸಮಾಂತರ ಕಿರಣ ನಾಭಿ F ಮೂಲಕ ಪ್ರತಿಫಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ (ಪೀನ ದರ್ಪಣದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಲ್ಲಿಂದ ಬಂದಂತೆ); ಧ್ರುವಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗುವ ಕಿರಣ ಸಮ ಕೋನದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರತಿಫಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಅವು ಬಿಂಬದಲ್ಲಿ ಸೇರುತ್ತವೆ: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, m = −v/u.

text.en: Object at F: image at infinity

tryThis.en: Concave mirror: bring the object from far away to F. How does the image change?
tryThis.kn: ನಿಮ್ನ ದರ್ಪಣ: ವಸ್ತುವನ್ನು ದೂರದಿಂದ F ಗೆ ತನ್ನಿ. ಬಿಂಬ ಹೇಗೆ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ?

tryThis.en: Put the object between F and the mirror. Where is the image and is it real?
tryThis.kn: ವಸ್ತುವನ್ನು F ಮತ್ತು ದರ್ಪಣದ ನಡುವೆ ಇಡಿ. ಬಿಂಬ ಎಲ್ಲಿ, ನೈಜವೇ?

tryThis.en: Switch to convex. Can you ever get a real image?
tryThis.kn: ಪೀನಕ್ಕೆ ಬದಲಿಸಿ. ನೈಜ ಬಿಂಬ ಎಂದಾದರೂ ಸಿಗುತ್ತದೆಯೇ?

say.en: Drag the tip of the object. A ray parallel to the axis reflects through the focus F (or seems to come from it, for a convex mirror); a ray to the pole reflects at an equal angle. They meet at the image: 1 over v plus 1 over u equals 1 over f, m equals -v over u. Cartesian signs: distances to the left of the mirror are negative.

body.en: The object distance $u$, image distance $v$ and focal length $f$ are related by $1/v + 1/u = 1/f$. The linear *magnification* is $m = h'/h = -v/u$. A negative $m$ means a real, inverted image; a positive $m$ means a virtual, erect image.
body.kn: ದರ್ಪಣ ಸಮೀಕರಣ 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. ವರ್ಧನೆ m = −v/u. m ಋಣವಾದರೆ ನೈಜ, ತಲೆಕೆಳಗಾದ ಬಿಂಬ; ಧನವಾದರೆ ಮಿಥ್ಯ, ನೇರ ಬಿಂಬ.

narration.en: The object distance u, image distance v and focal length f are related by 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. The linear magnification is m = h'/h = -v/u. A negative m means a real, inverted image; a positive m means a virtual, erect image.
narration.kn: ದರ್ಪಣ ಸಮೀಕರಣ 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. ವರ್ಧನೆ m = −v/u. m ಋಣವಾದರೆ ನೈಜ, ತಲೆಕೆಳಗಾದ ಬಿಂಬ; ಧನವಾದರೆ ಮಿಥ್ಯ, ನೇರ ಬಿಂಬ.

say.en: The object distance u, image distance v and focal length f are related by 1 over v plus 1 over u equals 1 over f. The linear magnification is m equals h'/h equals -v over u. A negative m means a real, inverted image; a positive m means a virtual, erect image. m is less than 0: real and inverted.
say.kn: ದರ್ಪಣ ಸಮೀಕರಣ 1 over v plus 1 over u equals 1 over f. ವರ್ಧನೆ m equals -v over u. m ಋಣವಾದರೆ ನೈಜ, ತಲೆಕೆಳಗಾದ ಬಿಂಬ; ಧನವಾದರೆ ಮಿಥ್ಯ, ನೇರ ಬಿಂಬ.

say.en: m is greater than 0: virtual and erect.
|m| is greater than 1: magnified.

caption.en: A concave mirror: move the object and watch where the image forms and how its size changes.
caption.kn: ನಿಮ್ನ ದರ್ಪಣ: ವಸ್ತುವನ್ನು ಸರಿಸಿ ಬಿಂಬ ಎಲ್ಲಿ ರೂಪುಗೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಅದರ ಗಾತ್ರ ಹೇಗೆ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ ನೋಡಿ.

tryThis.en: Bring the object inside the focus: the image jumps behind the mirror and becomes erect.
tryThis.kn: ವಸ್ತುವನ್ನು ನಾಭಿಯೊಳಗೆ ತನ್ನಿ: ಬಿಂಬ ದರ್ಪಣದ ಹಿಂದಕ್ಕೆ ಜಿಗಿದು ನೇರವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

tryThis.en: Place it at the centre of curvature: the image is the same size and inverted.

aim.en: To find the focal length of a concave mirror by plotting graphs between u and v and between 1/u and 1/v. Try this: On the 1/v against 1/u graph read both intercepts: each equals 1/f.
aim.kn: u ಮತ್ತು v ನಡುವೆ ಹಾಗೂ 1/u ಮತ್ತು 1/v ನಡುವೆ ಗ್ರಾಫ್ ರೇಖಿಸಿ ನಿಮ್ನ ದರ್ಪಣದ ನಾಭಿದೂರ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯುವುದು. ಇದನ್ನು ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ: 1/u ವಿರುದ್ಧ 1/v ಗ್ರಾಫ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಎರಡೂ ಅಂತಃಖಂಡಗಳನ್ನು ಓದಿ: ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದೂ 1/f ಗೆ ಸಮ.

aim.en: To find the focal length of a convex mirror using a convex lens. Try this: A convex mirror alone forms only virtual images, so let a convex lens send converging light at it. Move the mirror until the image coincides with the object needle: the rays then strike the mirror normally, so R = P − M and f = R/2.
aim.kn: ಪೀನ ಮಸೂರದ ಸಹಾಯದಿಂದ ಪೀನ ದರ್ಪಣದ ನಾಭಿದೂರ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯುವುದು. ಇದನ್ನು ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ: ಪೀನ ದರ್ಪಣ ಒಂದೇ ಕಾಲ್ಪನಿಕ ಬಿಂಬಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ರೂಪಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಪೀನ ಮಸೂರ ಅಭಿಸರಿಸುವ ಬೆಳಕನ್ನು ಅದರತ್ತ ಕಳುಹಿಸಲಿ. ಬಿಂಬ ವಸ್ತು ಸೂಜಿಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹೊಂದಿಕೆಯಾಗುವವರೆಗೆ ದರ್ಪಣ ಸರಿಸಿ: ಆಗ ಕಿರಣಗಳು ದರ್ಪಣಕ್ಕೆ ಲಂಬವಾಗಿ ಬೀಳುತ್ತವೆ, ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ R = P − M ಮತ್ತು f = R/2.

say.kn: ವರ್ಚುವಲ್ ಪ್ರಯೋಗಾಲಯ. ಪೀನ ಮಸೂರದ ಸಹಾಯದಿಂದ ಪೀನ ದರ್ಪಣದ ನಾಭಿದೂರ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯುವುದು. ಇದನ್ನು ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ: ಪೀನ ದರ್ಪಣ ಒಂದೇ ಕಾಲ್ಪನಿಕ ಬಿಂಬಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ರೂಪಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಪೀನ ಮಸೂರ ಅಭಿಸರಿಸುವ ಬೆಳಕನ್ನು ಅದರತ್ತ ಕಳುಹಿಸಲಿ. ಬಿಂಬ ವಸ್ತು ಸೂಜಿಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹೊಂದಿಕೆಯಾಗುವವರೆಗೆ ದರ್ಪಣ ಸರಿಸಿ: ಆಗ ಕಿರಣಗಳು ದರ್ಪಣಕ್ಕೆ ಲಂಬವಾಗಿ ಬೀಳುತ್ತವೆ, ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ R equals P - M ಮತ್ತು f equals R over 2.

tagline.en: Laws of reflection, the Cartesian sign convention, f = R/2, the mirror equation and magnification, and image formation by concave and convex mirrors.

myth.en: A concave mirror converges light, so its focal length is positive.

truth.en: In the NCERT Cartesian convention a concave mirror has a negative focal length and a convex mirror a positive one. The sign depends on where F lies, not on whether the mirror converges. Light falls on the mirror from the left, so the focus of a concave mirror lies against the incident direction and is negative.

say.en: The laws of reflection hold at every point of a curved mirror; the normal is the radius.
For paraxial rays $f = R/2$. Concave: $f < 0$; convex: $f > 0$ (NCERT convention).
Mirror equation $\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$; magnification $m = -\frac{v}{u}$.
m negative → real and inverted; m positive → virtual and erect.
Convex mirrors give diminished erect images and a wide field of view, so they are used as rear-view mirrors.

goal.en: Laws of reflection, the Cartesian sign convention, f = R/2, the mirror equation and magnification, and image formation by concave and convex mirrors.

task.en: Is the image real and inverted, or virtual and erect?

explain.en: For a real object, a concave mirror gives a real, inverted image unless the object is inside the focus. A convex mirror and a plane mirror always give virtual, erect images. Real images have m < 0, virtual images m > 0.

takeaway.en: The laws of reflection hold at every point of a curved mirror; the normal is the radius.

narration.en: Many people think: A concave mirror converges light, so its focal length is positive. Actually: In the NCERT Cartesian convention a concave mirror has a negative focal length and a convex mirror a positive one. The sign depends on where F lies, not on whether the mirror converges. Light falls on the mirror from the left, so the focus of a concave mirror lies against the incident direction and is negative.

problem.en: An object is 20 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the position, magnification and nature of the image.

answer.en: v = 60 cm in front; real, inverted, 3 times magnified

narration.en: Let us solve this together. An object is 20 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the position, magnification and nature of the image.

say.en: Let us solve this together. An object is 20 centimetres in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 centimetres. Find the position, magnification and nature of the image.
u equals minus 20 centimetres, f equals minus 15 centimetres.
1 over v equals 1 over f minus 1 over u equals minus 1 over 15 plus 1 over 20 equals minus 1 over 60, so v equals minus 60 centimetres.
m equals -v over u equals -minus 60/minus 20 equals minus 3.
So the answer is v equals 60 centimetres in front; real, inverted, 3 times magnified.

problem.en: An object is 20 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 20 cm. Find the image.

answer.en: 10 cm behind the mirror; virtual, erect, half size

narration.en: Let us solve this together. An object is 20 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 20 cm. Find the image.

say.en: Let us solve this together. An object is 20 centimetres in front of a convex mirror of focal length 20 centimetres. Find the image.
u equals minus 20 centimetres, f = plus 20 centimetres.
1 over v equals 1 over 20 plus 1 over 20 equals 1 over 10, so v = plus 10 centimetres.
m equals -v over u equals minus 10 over minus 20 = plus 0.5.
So the answer is 10 centimetres behind the mirror; virtual, erect, half size.

body.en: Real is negative, virtual is positive for mirrors: a real image (in front) has v < 0 and m < 0. If your answer for a convex mirror gives a real image, a sign has slipped.
